terms.gloss: the rights of a citizen, citizenship
evidence: Cic. Arch. 5.11; Cic. Caecin. 34.98 (Lewis & Short s.v. jūs: “the right to obtain the privileges of citizenship”)
terms.comment: The rights that go with citizenship, as a whole; Cicero uses it of the status a man could hold or lose. Rights in the modern political sense have no single ancient name.

evidence: Cic. Top. 18: sē capite dēminuere (Lewis & Short s.v. dēminuō)

terms.gloss: civil rights (Traupman); classically the civil law
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.39: novī cīvīlia jūra (Lewis & Short s.v. cīvīlis, under jūs cīvīle)
terms.comment: Classically jūs cīvīle and its plural cīvīlia jūra are the civil law, the private law of the state (see civil), so a reader would take the phrase in that sense.

phrases.english: to deprive someone of civil rights
phrases.source: Traupman 194; cf. Cic. Top. 18 (Lewis & Short s.v. dēminuō)

sources: Lewis & Short: jus · Lewis & Short: caput · Lewis & Short: deminuo
